subject: Unexpected tenant throttles during Nov 20 surge — reconciliation and credit proposal
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@kalypto.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@kalypto.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden surge -> many 429s for tenant 'kalypto-prod'

Hi Stephanie —

We started seeing a sharp uptick in token usage at ~08:50 PST this morning and began receiving intermittent 429s across our production traffic (tenant: kalypto-prod). Latency is spiking, and a subset of requests are failing fast. We rolled back a recent client-side change and still see errors.

Attached are a small sample of request IDs and timestamps from our side, plus a short HAR of a failing call. Can Redwood confirm whether this was a service-side enforcement (rate cap, quota window, or routing) or something on our end? This affected several user flows — our CS team is already getting tickets.

Request samples (from our logs):
- req_20261120_0853a (2026-11-20T08:53:21Z) 429 quota_exceeded
- req_20261120_0901b (2026-11-20T09:01:04Z) 429 rate_limit

We need visibility ASAP and an ETA for mitigation. Please advise next steps and whether credits will be offered for the outage.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Integrations, Kalypto, Inc.
attachments: kalypto-request-samples.csv, sample-failing-call.har

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@kalypto.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden surge -> many 429s for tenant 'kalypto-prod'

Hi Marta —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. We're sorry for the disruption. I chatted with infra and the initial signal shows an enforcement spike tied to a misapplied tenant window translation during an autoscale burst — effectively a narrower burst-window was applied to kalypto-prod for ~9:00–10:10 PST which caused premature rejections for short, high-concurrency bursts.

Immediate actions we have performed:
- Rolled back the window-override rule for kalypto-prod at 09:32 PST — that removed the enforcement restriction.
- Cleared the tenant prefix cache to ensure no stale routing keys persisted.
- Scoped a read-only diagnostic snapshot and attached it for your review (see drive link in this thread).

Next steps we propose:
1) Short-term: we will issue a corrective credit for the affected window and provide a formal post-incident impact summary by Monday.
2) Medium-term: update our deployment gating to add an automated canary for window-translations on tenant-scoped rules.
3) Ops follow-up call: we'd like to propose a 30-minute sync today at 11:00 PST — does that work for you?

I've looped in Neha (support lead) and Aditya (runtime) who are owning the technical follow-up. Expect a separate note with a proposed credit amount shortly.

Apologies again — we take these events seriously and will share full RCA.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
attachments: redwood-diagnostic-snapshot-20261120.tar.gz

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Kalypto burst -> corrective credits + customer comms

Team —

Summary: Kalypto-prod experienced 429s due to a deployment that accidentally applied a tighter burst-window to the tenant. Incident window ~08:50–09:32 PST; residual failures for ~till 10:10 as queues drained. Customer reports impact to user-facing flows — CS notified.

Please action the following: 
- Neha: prepare a credit proposal (recurring usage impact + one-time goodwill). Start with an estimate of 6 hours of affected traffic at their SOW per-token rate and include a one-off $3,000 goodwill credit for customer experience. Deliver draft PDF by EOD.
- Aditya: capture the exact kernel selection and rule-change diff from the deployment at 08:45–09:00; include timeline and config lines. Add a mitigation checklist for engineering (canary gating + auto-rollback guard).
- Evelyn: coordinate the 11:00 PST ops call invite and ensure CS is briefed.

Keep communications conservative: no admission of systemic billing fault beyond this specific mis-translation. We'll provide logs, timeline, and the credit proposal. I will lead the customer call.

Thanks —
Stephanie

On Fri, 20 Nov 2026 at 09:45 Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the quick heads-up... (see above)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@kalypto.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident: timeline, evidence, and credit proposal for Kalypto-prod enforcement spike

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the internal review. Below is a concise impact summary and the remediation items we are delivering: 

What happened:
- A deployment change pushed on 2026-11-20 08:47 PST inadvertently set a tenant-specific enforcement window to 50% of the intended burst. This caused premature 429s for short bursts between ~08:50–09:32 PST.

Customer impact (our estimate):
- Affected time window: 2026-11-20T08:50:00–2026-11-20T09:32:00 PST
- Estimated failed requests: ~1,320 (based on combined telemetry + your samples)
- User-facing errors: intermittent across your webhooks and real-time flows; CS reported ~48 tickets during the window.

What we did:
- Rolled back the window-override at 09:32 PST (remediation).
- Delivered diagnostic traces and request-id mappings to your team (Drive link).
- Implemented an automated canary for window translation changes and tightened rollout gating.

Compensation proposal:
- Corrective usage credit: equivalent to 8 hours of typical token consumption at your committed SOW rate (covers conservative over-estimate).
- One-time goodwill credit: $3,000 applied to your next invoice.
- Attached: redwood-credit-proposal-20261122.pdf with the credit math and how it'll appear on billing.

Attachments: kalypto-ratecap-evidence.zip (request-id mapping, internal enforcement traces), redwood-credit-proposal-20261122.pdf

Next steps we suggest:
1) Confirm whether the proposed credit covers your reconciliation needs.
2) Accept the DocuSign (if needed) or confirm by reply and we'll apply to the upcoming invoice.
3) Optional: join a 30-minute RCA call next week to review technical remediation and long-term controls.

We regret the disruption and appreciate you raising this quickly — we'll follow with a full RCA doc in Confluence by Monday and the remediation tickets in our backlog with target SLAs.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
